data.revised_prompt:
Create a publication-quality flat vector infographic on a white background in a clean journal-ready style, 16:9 landscape. Title at top: “Satellite Embedding: A Review”. Use a subtle earth-tone palette only: dark green, deep blue, warm ochre, muted gray. No 3D, no shadows, no cartoon style, no decorative clutter. All labels in English, concise, readable at paper scale, aligned with consistent typography.

Layout: central hub labeled “Satellite Embeddings” in the middle. Four main branches radiate with thin arrows and clean connectors showing flow from left to top to right to bottom: Data Space -> Model Families -> Representation Types -> Applications. Add arrows between the branches to indicate this flow.

LEFT BRANCH: heading “Data Space” with small simple line icons and labels arranged vertically or in a neat grid: optical, SAR, multispectral, hyperspectral, coarse-resolution, temporal series, multimodal fusion. Use tiny abstract icons (e.g., satellite image tile, radar wave, stacked bands, spectral prism bars, pixel grid, time axis, combined sensors) but keep them minimal and flat.

TOP BRANCH: heading “Model Families” with five color-coded grouped boxes or pills, each distinct but consistent: precomputed embedding products, vision-language models, masked autoencoder family, multimodal generalist EO encoders, application-specialized EO encoders. Use a restrained palette variation within the earth-tone scheme.

RIGHT BRANCH: heading “Representation Types” with five compact nodes: pooled scene vector, dense token grid, annual embedding field, image-text joint space, multimodal latent space.

BOTTOM BRANCH: heading “Applications” with six nodes: land-cover classification, water extraction, crop monitoring, regression/mapping, retrieval, multimodal analysis.

Add a small side legend labeled “Key axes” listing four items with minimalist bullets: modality, temporal semantics, spatial scale, deployment mode.

Overall design should feel like a polished academic review figure: balanced spacing, strong alignment, crisp vector edges, thin lines, no clutter, highly legible, minimal but informative, suitable for inclusion in a paper review article.
